2.translation: Identify the original input and the intended plot. Every path preserves source IDs, complete lengths and coordinate units. Readers do not run alignments or generate missing relationships or annotations.

3.translation: | Input available | Shortest processing path | Result and plotting entry |

5.translation: | Existing R tables | Organize [minimal fields](⟦shared:0⟧), check endpoint/annotation IDs and inspect [validation reports](⟦shared:1⟧) | Length, HSP and annotation tables → [shared data and layers](⟦shared:2⟧) |

6.translation: | FASTA, GFF3 and BLAST/PAF | [Import sequences and annotations](⟦shared:0⟧), then [alignments](⟦shared:1⟧); check lengths, units and IDs, retaining reverse endpoints | Source tables → [relationship plot](⟦shared:2⟧) or [HSP Dotplot](⟦shared:3⟧) |

7.translation: | One GenBank record | Use ⟦shared:1⟧ in [sequence import](⟦shared:0⟧); inspect lengths, annotation hierarchy and original segments | One sequence and annotations → [circular backbone and annotations](⟦shared:2⟧) |

8.translation: | Protein BLASTp and complete lengths | [Declare aa units and read alignments](⟦shared:0⟧); verify both protein IDs; supply actual CDS/phase before projecting to DNA | Protein positions → [protein comparison](⟦shared:0⟧); DNA positions → [projection](⟦shared:1⟧) |

9.translation: | BED/BEDPE intervals | [Read intervals or paired intervals](⟦shared:0⟧) and check the reader's one-based conversion without converting twice | Annotation intervals or paired links → [features](⟦shared:1⟧) and [links](⟦shared:2⟧) |

10.translation: | bedGraph/BigWig signals | [Import signals](⟦shared:0⟧), retaining units, missingness and source intervals without filling unknown regions with zero | Signals → [tracks](⟦shared:1⟧); counts/bins → [track statistics](⟦shared:2⟧) |

11.translation: | Existing character alignment | [Import aligned characters](⟦shared:0⟧), checking gaps, source positions and alphabet | Observed alignment columns → [magnification and character details](⟦shared:1⟧) |

14.translation: 1. Sequence ⟦shared:0⟧ values are unique and lengths come from complete sources, never the last annotation endpoint.

15.translation: 2. Link ⟦shared:0⟧/⟦shared:1⟧ and annotation ⟦shared:2⟧ match the sequence table. Explicitly distinguish repeated contig names across samples; readers do not guess membership.

16.translation: 3. DNA uses bp and proteins use aa; BED/PAF readers already convert coordinates. Ascending/descending link endpoints can encode direction and must not be uniformly sorted.

17.translation: 4. Draw a minimal plot before adding layers, [local settings](⟦shared:0⟧) and [target-size output](⟦shared:1⟧). Use [symptom-based diagnostics](⟦shared:2⟧) for problems.

20.translation: [Sequence comparison from FASTA/GFF3/BLAST](⟦shared:0⟧) retains paths, display filters, inputs and results. Obtain originals from the [input archive](⟦shared:1⟧), extract it and run downloaded scripts from a directory containing ⟦shared:2⟧.

21.translation: ## Choose the operation by its output ⟦shared:0⟧

22.translation: | Desired result | Entry point and interpretation |

24.translation: | Local tables, several windows, or an overview with details | ⟦shared:0⟧ clips to a local interval. ⟦shared:1⟧ prepares windows, which can represent one source row more than once when they overlap. ⟦shared:2⟧ returns an overview and detail composition. A clipped HSP length estimates the displayed span. See [local views](⟦shared:3⟧). |

25.translation: | Move a feature or its text | ⟦shared:0⟧ allocates lanes to overlapping features. See [label layout](⟦shared:1⟧) for placing an individual label and for automatic placement of a group. |

26.translation: | Select or summarize links | Filtering keeps qualifying rows, deduplication selects representatives, interval merging produces new boundaries, and bundling records bin members. In plots, ⟦shared:0⟧ is normalized by the largest bin weight within the sequence pair and expresses relative density. See [ribbon statistics](⟦shared:1⟧). |
